metadata.title: JZ Mock A · Paper 2
metadata.description: Worked steps, progressive hints and reviewed follow-up questions.

matches.rationale: Both find the full parameter set giving one distinct cubic root from the turning heights, then distinguish a sufficient subset from a necessary condition.
sharedKnowledge: Both find the full parameter set giving one distinct cubic root from the turning heights, then distinguish a sufficient subset from a necessary condition.

matches.rationale: Both use derivative turning heights and strict axis-crossing conditions to constrain a cubic parameter. The candidate requests three roots directly; the original additionally compares one-root conditions for sufficiency.
sharedKnowledge: Both use derivative turning heights and strict axis-crossing conditions to constrain a cubic parameter. The candidate requests three roots directly; the original additionally compares one-root conditions for sufficiency.

matches.rationale: Both divide a polynomial expression by a radical power, rewrite as a sum of fractional powers and apply the elementary power rule. The candidate asks for the derivative formula rather than its value at a point.
sharedKnowledge: Both divide a polynomial expression by a radical power, rewrite as a sum of fractional powers and apply the elementary power rule. The candidate asks for the derivative formula rather than its value at a point.

matches.rationale: Both rewrite a radical quotient into fractional-power terms, differentiate and evaluate the gradient at a specified positive input.
sharedKnowledge: Both rewrite a radical quotient into fractional-power terms, differentiate and evaluate the gradient at a specified positive input.

matches.rationale: Both expand a powered numerator and divide termwise by a fractional power before differentiating; the candidate requests the resulting formula rather than a numerical gradient.
sharedKnowledge: Both expand a powered numerator and divide termwise by a fractional power before differentiating; the candidate requests the resulting formula rather than a numerical gradient.

matches.rationale: Both audit a chain of square/quadratic inequality transformations and check whether the final range follows. The candidate starts with a quartic square, while the original must first justify squaring a nonnegative radical inequality.
sharedKnowledge: Both audit a chain of square/quadratic inequality transformations and check whether the final range follows. The candidate starts with a quartic square, while the original must first justify squaring a nonnegative radical inequality.

matches.rationale: Both audit whether a squaring step preserves the original inequality and its sign conditions. The candidate supplies a trig setting where a negative branch invalidates the step; the original has a domain that makes the squaring reversible.
sharedKnowledge: Both audit whether a squaring step preserves the original inequality and its sign conditions. The candidate supplies a trig setting where a negative branch invalidates the step; the original has a domain that makes the squaring reversible.

matches.rationale: Both inspect given integer values and require the divisibility premise to hold while the asserted divisibility conclusion fails.
sharedKnowledge: Both inspect given integer values and require the divisibility premise to hold while the asserted divisibility conclusion fails.

matches.rationale: Both find genuine integer counterexamples by checking a number-theoretic premise and a false conclusion. The candidate requires enumerating residue classes and nonprimes; the original checks a supplied short list for square divisibility.
sharedKnowledge: Both find genuine integer counterexamples by checking a number-theoretic premise and a false conclusion. The candidate requires enumerating residue classes and nonprimes; the original checks a supplied short list for square divisibility.

matches.rationale: Both locate the first invalid inference that a multiple of3 must be composite, overlooking the prime value3 itself.
sharedKnowledge: Both locate the first invalid inference that a multiple of3 must be composite, overlooking the prime value3 itself.

matches.rationale: Both decide which inequalities follow for ordered negative reals by recording the sign of the actual multiplier or divisor and reversing the direction when needed.
sharedKnowledge: Both decide which inequalities follow for ordered negative reals by recording the sign of the actual multiplier or divisor and reversing the direction when needed.

matches.rationale: Both test universal ordered-real inequalities using monotonic fixed-base exponentials and valid counterexamples. The candidate adds sums/quotients of powers; the original also tests negative products and a reciprocal crossing zero.
sharedKnowledge: Both test universal ordered-real inequalities using monotonic fixed-base exponentials and valid counterexamples. The candidate adds sums/quotients of powers; the original also tests negative products and a reciprocal crossing zero.

matches.rationale: Both impose positivity of an upward quadratic for every real input by making its discriminant strictly negative. The candidate isolates one quadratic; the original must intersect the two conditions created by a modulus.
sharedKnowledge: Both impose positivity of an upward quadratic for every real input by making its discriminant strictly negative. The candidate isolates one quadratic; the original must intersect the two conditions created by a modulus.

matches.rationale: Both determine every parameter for which a modulus inequality holds for all real inputs, proving necessity and sufficiency and checking boundary equality. The candidate compares two piecewise-linear modulus graphs; the original compares a modulus with a quadratic.
sharedKnowledge: Both determine every parameter for which a modulus inequality holds for all real inputs, proving necessity and sufficiency and checking boundary equality. The candidate compares two piecewise-linear modulus graphs; the original compares a modulus with a quadratic.

matches.rationale: Both extract coordinate consequences from simultaneous two-variable inequalities and verify a feasible point before calling it a counterexample. The candidate has two straight boundaries; the original combines a parabolic band with a line.
sharedKnowledge: Both extract coordinate consequences from simultaneous two-variable inequalities and verify a feasible point before calling it a counterexample. The candidate has two straight boundaries; the original combines a parabolic band with a line.

matches.rationale: Both test universal claims over the intersection of line and parabolic inequalities by constructing points that satisfy both hypotheses while violating a claimed bound.
sharedKnowledge: Both test universal claims over the intersection of line and parabolic inequalities by constructing points that satisfy both hypotheses while violating a claimed bound.

matches.rationale: Both determine whether a trigonometric signed integral vanishes exactly at the stated periodic endpoints, then classify necessity and sufficiency. The candidate has one sine integrand; the original additionally needs a comparison preventing cancellation between two accumulated integrals.
sharedKnowledge: Both determine whether a trigonometric signed integral vanishes exactly at the stated periodic endpoints, then classify necessity and sufficiency. The candidate has one sine integrand; the original additionally needs a comparison preventing cancellation between two accumulated integrals.

matches.rationale: Both use reflection about the correct interval centre to prove signed-area cancellation and distinguish sufficient conditions from weaker unsupported claims. The candidate isolates antisymmetry; the original also needs to rule out other zero endpoints.
sharedKnowledge: Both use reflection about the correct interval centre to prove signed-area cancellation and distinguish sufficient conditions from weaker unsupported claims. The candidate isolates antisymmetry; the original also needs to rule out other zero endpoints.

matches.rationale: Both analyse a logarithm whose base varies with the horizontal input by converting to exponential or fixed-base form. The candidate restricts to bases above1; the original additionally compares the two sides of the forbidden base1.
sharedKnowledge: Both analyse a logarithm whose base varies with the horizontal input by converting to exponential or fixed-base form. The candidate restricts to bases above1; the original additionally compares the two sides of the forbidden base1.

matches.rationale: Both use sin²x+cos²x=1, factor and cancel a rational expression in cosine, then use its exact attainable range to optimise a positive reciprocal.
sharedKnowledge: Both use sin²x+cos²x=1, factor and cancel a rational expression in cosine, then use its exact attainable range to optimise a positive reciprocal.

matches.rationale: Both evaluate a parameter-dependent cubic at a classified stationary input and impose strict height conditions with boundary checks. The candidate uses the minimum to count positive intersections; the original uses the minimum coordinates to enforce a quadrant.
sharedKnowledge: Both evaluate a parameter-dependent cubic at a classified stationary input and impose strict height conditions with boundary checks. The candidate uses the minimum to count positive intersections; the original uses the minimum coordinates to enforce a quadrant.

matches.rationale: Both unfold adjacent equilateral faces of a solid, place points in the resulting plane and compare valid surface routes using exact right-triangle distances. The candidate is a square pyramid; the original is a regular tetrahedron.
sharedKnowledge: Both unfold adjacent equilateral faces of a solid, place points in the resulting plane and compare valid surface routes using exact right-triangle distances. The candidate is a square pyramid; the original is a regular tetrahedron.

matches.rationale: Both distinguish a statement’s contrapositive from its converse or inverse when deciding what a supplied implication guarantees. The candidate isolates implication direction; the original additionally negates nested AND/OR conditions.
sharedKnowledge: Both distinguish a statement’s contrapositive from its converse or inverse when deciding what a supplied implication guarantees. The candidate isolates implication direction; the original additionally negates nested AND/OR conditions.

matches.rationale: Both locate a first invalid line in an integer divisibility proof by checking a missing strict range restriction. The candidate requires a remainder smaller than the divisor; the original requires factorial factors smaller than its upper endpoint.
sharedKnowledge: Both locate a first invalid line in an integer divisibility proof by checking a missing strict range restriction. The candidate requires a remainder smaller than the divisor; the original requires factorial factors smaller than its upper endpoint.

matches.rationale: Both convert linked logarithms into powers or common-base ratios and cancel a cyclic logarithm product subject to nonzero base logarithms. The candidate calculates a third logarithm; the original additionally uses positivity to reach a contradiction.
sharedKnowledge: Both convert linked logarithms into powers or common-base ratios and cancel a cyclic logarithm product subject to nonzero base logarithms. The candidate calculates a third logarithm; the original additionally uses positivity to reach a contradiction.

matches.rationale: Both split a ceiling-function integral into constant unit-width rectangles and evaluate a finite geometric sum with precise first/last indices. The original adds a linear weight and therefore requires shifting and subtracting the weighted series.
sharedKnowledge: Both split a ceiling-function integral into constant unit-width rectangles and evaluate a finite geometric sum with precise first/last indices. The original adds a linear weight and therefore requires shifting and subtracting the weighted series.

matches.rationale: Both retain every branch of a squared trigonometric equation and count all distinct roots on the stated interval with careful endpoints. The candidate has a triple-angle input; the original has an unknown strict integer upper endpoint and denominator exclusions.
sharedKnowledge: Both retain every branch of a squared trigonometric equation and count all distinct roots on the stated interval with careful endpoints. The candidate has a triple-angle input; the original has an unknown strict integer upper endpoint and denominator exclusions.

matches.rationale: Both replace a quadratic identity in cosine by a bounded algebraic equation and recover all valid angle branches. The candidate isolates modulus and cosine range recovery; the original additionally requires domain checks, double-angle factorisation and extended root counting.
sharedKnowledge: Both replace a quadratic identity in cosine by a bounded algebraic equation and recover all valid angle branches. The candidate isolates modulus and cosine range recovery; the original additionally requires domain checks, double-angle factorisation and extended root counting.

matches.rationale: Both reduce a squared trigonometric equation to a bounded algebraic problem and recover all distinct trig roots, retaining both signs and counting closed endpoints correctly. The original additionally has a strict unknown upper bound and denominator restrictions.
sharedKnowledge: Both reduce a squared trigonometric equation to a bounded algebraic problem and recover all distinct trig roots, retaining both signs and counting closed endpoints correctly. The original additionally has a strict unknown upper bound and denominator restrictions.
